known.via: English Wikipedia "Côte Chalonnaise" (a wine place on Wikidata)

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Seasons this mild ripen Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Pinot Gris, Gewürztraminer and Riesling fully without cooking off their freshness.
Chardonnay and Pinot Noir sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

soil.rock: Limestone makes alkaline soil that drains well yet can hold water for the vines. It is usually planted to grapes valued for their acidity. Gravel drains fast and is poor, so roots go deep for water and food. It holds little water.
soil.top: The topsoil drains well and still stores water for dry spells, so vines grow evenly. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.
